module.title: Days 1–10 | Competition Mastery Module
module.description: Production candidate: authored topic-driven National English Championship curriculum.

lessons.title: Advanced vocabulary
lessons.objective: Build competition-ready understanding of advanced vocabulary and apply it accurately to unfamiliar questions.
lessons.core_teaching_content: Advanced English competition work combines vocabulary, grammar, close reading, argument, literary technique and precise editing. Interpret language in context and support claims with textual evidence. Tone and register depend on audience, purpose and wording. For difficult options, ask which choice is most exact rather than merely acceptable. Distractors often contain a true statement that fails to answer the specific question. In this lesson, focus specifically on advanced vocabulary. Identify the defining concepts, the distinctions that commonly cause mistakes, and the evidence or procedure needed to justify an answer. Practise moving from recognition to application: first identify what the question is testing, then select a method, perform the reasoning carefully, and verify the result against the wording and constraints. Keep an error log that records the misconception or decision error, not just the correct answer.
examples: A National English Championship question on advanced vocabulary should be solved by identifying the key clue, applying the relevant principle, and checking the option against all stated conditions.
Create a new advanced vocabulary scenario with one tempting distractor. Explain why the correct response is supported and why the distractor fails.
lessons.practical_activity: Complete a focused National English Championship activity on advanced vocabulary. Build a small table, diagram, worked example, speaking sample, writing sample or practice set as appropriate to the subject, then explain the reasoning behind the result.
lessons.guided_practice: Work through three scaffolded tasks on advanced vocabulary: model the first, prompt the second, and require independent justification on the third. Ask the learner to identify the exact clue, rule or evidence used before confirming the answer.
independent_practice: Solve three unfamiliar questions on advanced vocabulary without viewing the answer.
Create one new example and solve it using the lesson method.
Review one distractor or error and explain why it is wrong.
lessons.assessment_checkpoint: Complete an eight-item National English Championship checkpoint focused on advanced vocabulary. Target at least six correct and justify every uncertain response.
lessons.student_task: Produce one finished National English Championship task demonstrating advanced vocabulary and record the reasoning, evidence or performance criteria used.
lessons.tutor_guidance: Coach the learner toward evidence-based reasoning and precise terminology. Ask for the method before giving correction, and turn each error into a reusable rule or practice target. This lesson remains suitable for self-learning.
lessons.reflection_completion: Record one strength, one mistake pattern and one concrete action for improving advanced vocabulary in the next practice session.
lessons.daily_flow: Learn → Worked Example → Guided Practice → Independent Practice → Check → Reflect
